title: OpenAI Foundation awards $50m to 163 nonprofits exploring AI in local communities
key_facts: The OpenAI Foundation selected 163 US nonprofits to share $50 million through its 2026 People-First AI Fund, backing organisations exploring how AI could support community services, arts and culture, and local journalism.
Recipients are based across 35 states and Washington DC, with work reaching all 50 states; the grants are unrestricted, so organisations decide how, or whether, AI tools fit their work.

It is the second People-First AI Fund, after an initial $50 million round in 2025; the Foundation received 1,669 applications, each reviewed by an external grantmaker, and judged community trust, demonstrated impact and how applicants proposed to explore AI.
All 163 grants are expected to be paid in full before the end of 2026; most 2026 recipients are new to the fund.

Examples in community services: Rural Opportunity Institute (North Carolina), which the Foundation says helped partner schools double Medicaid revenue and triple the number of students receiving mental health services; Greater Bakersfield Legal Assistance (AI for intake and multilingual resources); JustFix (tools to help renters understand records and eviction).
Arts: Nashville Jazz Workshop plans a searchable concert archive and an AI listening companion; the August Wilson African American Cultural Center is looking at AI for administrative work.

Journalism: Honolulu Civil Beat is making Hawaii legislature records easier to search; California Black Media, Free Press Indiana, the American Journalism Project and the Colorado News Collaborative (about 200 local news organisations) are also grantees.
The fund is not tied to OpenAI products; the Foundation says recipients can choose any platform or decide not to use one.
